message.content:
Project under review: /workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management (a RISC-V bare-metal OS lab, SV39 paging, 2 harts, global kernel lock).
The newly written code is in kernel/mm/mm.c, kernel/sched/sched.c and include/os/mm.h (see `cd /workspace && git diff`).
Everything else in the tree is given/unmodifiable context: init/main.c, arch/riscv/kernel/{entry.S,boot.c,start.S}, arch/riscv/include/pgtable.h, include/os/{sched.h,elf.h,mm.h}, kernel/irq/irq.c, kernel/syscall/syscall.c, drivers/screen.c, test/*.c, tiny_libc/.
Key facts you must verify against the real files rather than assume:
- user ELFs link at 0x10000 but their PT_LOAD segment starts at vaddr 0xf000 (headers included), memsz up to ~0x3e98.
- USER_STACK_ADDR = 0xf00010000, PGDIR_PA = 0x5e000000, kernel window VPN2 = 0x101, KERNEL_MEM_OFFSET = 0xffffffc000000000.
- main.c init_pcb() loads the shell with load_elf(..., get_kva_of) which only WALKS the page table, so init_page_table() must pre-map the code pages.
- main.c's idle loop frees each exited task's kernel stack with free_user_page(kva2pa(kernel_stack_base - PAGE_SIZE)).
- there is no satp switch in entry.S, so scheduler() must do it.
Only report defects in the NEW code. Do not report pre-existing issues in given files unless the new code depends on them incorrectly.

LENS: shared memory and the page fault handler. Scrutinise shm_page_get(), shm_page_dt(), handle_page_fault() in kernel/mm/mm.c against test/consensus.c which does: get -> dt -> write to the old address -> get again and expects a DIFFERENT virtual address. Check: the reserved VA window and whether it collides with the ELF image at 0xf000 or the shm attach ever returns 0 for a valid mapping, reference counting across processes and across process exit (free_process_user_page), pinning, detaching an address that is not shared, the bounds check in handle_page_fault, faults on kernel addresses, and what happens on a fault while a page is on disk.

#include <asm.h>
#include <csr.h>

.macro SAVE_CONTEXT
  addi sp, sp, -(OFFSET_SIZE)
  /* 
   * save all general purpose registers
   * register $zero, $sp, $tp are not stored here! 
   */
  sd ra, OFFSET_REG_RA(sp)
  sd gp, OFFSET_REG_GP(sp)
  sd t0, OFFSET_REG_T0(sp)
  sd t1, OFFSET_REG_T1(sp)
  sd t2, OFFSET_REG_T2(sp)
  sd s0, OFFSET_REG_S0(sp)
  sd s1, OFFSET_REG_S1(sp)
  sd a0, OFFSET_REG_A0(sp)
  sd a1, OFFSET_REG_A1(sp)
  sd a2, OFFSET_REG_A2(sp)
  sd a3, OFFSET_REG_A3(sp)
  sd a4, OFFSET_REG_A4(sp)
  sd a5, OFFSET_REG_A5(sp)
  sd a6, OFFSET_REG_A6(sp)
  sd a7, OFFSET_REG_A7(sp)
  sd s2, OFFSET_REG_S2(sp)
  sd s3, OFFSET_REG_S3(sp)
  sd s4, OFFSET_REG_S4(sp)
  sd s5, OFFSET_REG_S5(sp)
  sd s6, OFFSET_REG_S6(sp)
  sd s7, OFFSET_REG_S7(sp)
  sd s8, OFFSET_REG_S8(sp)
  sd s9, OFFSET_REG_S9(sp)
  sd s10, OFFSET_REG_S10(sp)
  sd s11, OFFSET_REG_S11(sp)
  sd t3, OFFSET_REG_T3(sp)
  sd t4, OFFSET_REG_T4(sp)
  sd t5, OFFSET_REG_T5(sp)
  sd t6, OFFSET_REG_T6(sp)

  /* save sstatus, sepc, stval, scause, sscratch on kernel stack */
  csrr t0, CSR_SSTATUS
  sd t0, OFFSET_REG_SSTATUS(sp)
  csrr t0, CSR_SEPC
  sd t0, OFFSET_REG_SEPC(sp)
  csrr t0, CSR_STVAL
  sd t0, OFFSET_REG_STVAL(sp)
  csrr t0, CSR_SCAUSE
  sd t0, OFFSET_REG_SCAUSE(sp)
  csrr t0, CSR_SSCRATCH
  sd t0, OFFSET_REG_SSCRATCH(sp)

  sd sp, PCB_KERNEL_SP(tp)
.endm

.macro RESTORE_CONTEXT
  ld sp, PCB_KERNEL_SP(tp)
  /* 
   * restore all registers and sstatus, sepc, stval, scause, sscratch
   * register $zero, $sp, $tp are not restored here!
   */
  ld ra, OFFSET_REG_RA(sp)
  ld gp, OFFSET_REG_GP(sp)
  ld t0, OFFSET_REG_T0(sp)
  ld t1, OFFSET_REG_T1(sp)
  ld t2, OFFSET_REG_T2(sp)
  ld s0, OFFSET_REG_S0(sp)
  ld s1, OFFSET_REG_S1(sp)
  ld a0, OFFSET_REG_A0(sp)
  ld a1, OFFSET_REG_A1(sp)
  ld a2, OFFSET_REG_A2(sp)
  ld a3, OFFSET_REG_A3(sp)
  ld a4, OFFSET_REG_A4(sp)
  ld a5, OFFSET_REG_A5(sp)
  ld a6, OFFSET_REG_A6(sp)
  ld a7, OFFSET_REG_A7(sp)
  ld s2, OFFSET_REG_S2(sp)
  ld s3, OFFSET_REG_S3(sp)
  ld s4, OFFSET_REG_S4(sp)
  ld s5, OFFSET_REG_S5(sp)
  ld s6, OFFSET_REG_S6(sp)
  ld s7, OFFSET_REG_S7(sp)
  ld s8, OFFSET_REG_S8(sp)
  ld s9, OFFSET_REG_S9(sp)
  ld s10, OFFSET_REG_S10(sp)
  ld s11, OFFSET_REG_S11(sp)
  ld t3, OFFSET_REG_T3(sp)
  ld t4, OFFSET_REG_T4(sp)
  ld t5, OFFSET_REG_T5(sp)
  ld t6, OFFSET_REG_T6(sp)

  ld t0, OFFSET_REG_SSTATUS(sp)
  csrw CSR_SSTATUS, t0
  ld t0, OFFSET_REG_SEPC(sp)
  csrw CSR_SEPC, t0
  ld t0, OFFSET_REG_STVAL(sp)
  csrw CSR_STVAL, t0
  ld t0, OFFSET_REG_SCAUSE(sp)
  csrw CSR_SCAUSE, t0
  ld t0, OFFSET_REG_SSCRATCH(sp)
  csrw CSR_SSCRATCH, t0

  addi sp, sp, (OFFSET_SIZE)
  sd sp, PCB_KERNEL_SP(tp)
.endm

/* 
 * trick: during an irq handling, current_running may be modified
 * but $tp will not be modified until ret_from_exception()
 */
ENTRY(enable_preempt)
  ld t0, PCB_PREEMPT_COUNT(tp)
  beq t0, zero, do_enable
  addi t0, t0, -1
  sd t0, PCB_PREEMPT_COUNT(tp)
  beq t0, zero, do_enable
  jr ra
do_enable:
  not t0, x0
  csrs CSR_SIE, t0
  jr ra
ENDPROC(enable_preempt)

ENTRY(disable_preempt)
  csrw CSR_SIE, zero  
  ld t0, PCB_PREEMPT_COUNT(tp)
  addi t0, t0, 1
  sd t0, PCB_PREEMPT_COUNT(tp)
  jr ra
ENDPROC(disable_preempt)

ENTRY(enable_interrupt)
  li t0, SR_SIE
  csrs CSR_SSTATUS, t0
  jr ra
ENDPROC(enable_interrupt)

ENTRY(disable_interrupt)
  li t0, SR_SIE
  csrc CSR_SSTATUS, t0
  jr ra
ENDPROC(disable_interrupt)

ENTRY(enable_sum)
  li t0, SR_SUM
  csrs CSR_SSTATUS, t0
  jr ra
ENDPROC(enable_sum)

ENTRY(disable_sum)
  li t0, SR_SUM
  csrc CSR_SSTATUS, t0
  jr ra
ENDPROC(disable_sum)

ENTRY(ret_from_exception)
  ld tp, current_cpu_running
  call unlock_kernel
  RESTORE_CONTEXT

  csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp
  bnez tp, to_user
to_kernel:
  csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp
  ld sp, PCB_KERNEL_SP(tp)
  j restore_sp_done
to_user:
  ld sp, PCB_USER_SP(tp)
restore_sp_done:
  sret
ENDPROC(ret_from_exception)

ENTRY(exception_handler_entry)
  /* use kernel stack to handle exception */
  csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp
  bnez tp, from_user

from_kernel:
  csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp
  j store_sp_done
from_user:
  sd sp, PCB_USER_SP(tp)
  ld sp, PCB_KERNEL_SP(tp)
store_sp_done:

  SAVE_CONTEXT
  /* 
   * Disable user-mode memory access as it should only be set in the actual user copy routines.
   * Disable the FPU to detect illegal usage of floating point in kernel space.
   */
  li t0, SR_SUM | SR_FS
  csrc sstatus, t0

  /* load the global pointer */
  .option push
  .option norelax
  la gp, __global_pointer$
  .option pop

  call lock_kernel
  /* 
   * load ret_from_exception into $ra
   * so that we can return to ret_from_exception
   * when interrupt_helper complete.
   */
  la ra, ret_from_exception
  
  /* call interrupt_helper and pass parameters for it */
  mv a0, sp
  csrr a1, CSR_STVAL
  csrr a2, CSR_SCAUSE
  j interrupt_helper
ENDPROC(exception_handler_entry)

ENTRY(clear_ipi)
  li t0, SIE_SSIE
  csrc CSR_SIP, t0
  jr ra
ENDPROC(clear_ipi)

--- makefile
SHELL := /bin/bash
HOST_CC = gcc
CROSS_PREFIX = riscv64-unknown-linux-gnu-
CC = ${CROSS_PREFIX}gcc
AR = ${CROSS_PREFIX}ar
OBJDUMP = ${CROSS_PREFIX}objdump
CFLAGS = -O0 -nostdlib -T riscv.lds -Wall -mcmodel=medany -Iinclude -Idrivers -nostdinc -g -fvar-tracking -ffreestanding
USER_CFLAGS = -O0 -nostdlib -T user_riscv.lds -Wall -mcmodel=medany -Itest -Itiny_libc/include -Iinclude -nostdinc -g -fvar-tracking
USER_LDFLAGS = -L./ -ltiny_libc
DISK = /dev/sdb

BOOTLOADER_ENTRYPOINT = 0x50200000
START_ENTRYPOINT = 0x50201000
KERNEL_ENTRYPOINT = 0xffffffc050400000

ARCH = riscv
ARCH_DIR = ./arch/$(ARCH)
CFLAGS += -Iarch/$(ARCH)/include
USER_CFLAGS += -Iarch/$(ARCH)/include
USER_LDFLAGS += $(ARCH_DIR)/crt0.o

SRC_BOOT 	= $(ARCH_DIR)/boot/bootblock.S
SRC_HEAD    = $(ARCH_DIR)/kernel/head.S $(ARCH_DIR)/kernel/boot.c payload.c ./libs/string.c
SRC_ARCH	= $(ARCH_DIR)/kernel/trap.S $(ARCH_DIR)/kernel/entry.S $(ARCH_DIR)/kernel/start.S $(ARCH_DIR)/sbi/common.c $(ARCH_DIR)/kernel/smp.S
SRC_DRIVER	= ./drivers/screen.c
SRC_INIT 	= ./init/main.c
SRC_INT		= ./kernel/irq/irq.c
SRC_LOCK	= ./kernel/locking/lock.c ./kernel/locking/futex.c ./kernel/locking/binsem.c
SRC_SCHED	= ./kernel/sched/sched.c ./kernel/sched/time.c ./kernel/sched/smp.c
SRC_MM	    = ./kernel/mm/mm.c
SRC_SYSCALL	= ./kernel/syscall/syscall.c ./kernel/syscall/mailbox.c
SRC_LIBS	= ./libs/string.c ./libs/printk.c

SRC_LIBC	= ./tiny_libc/printf.c ./tiny_libc/string.c ./tiny_libc/mthread.c ./tiny_libc/syscall.c ./tiny_libc/invoke_syscall.S \
				./tiny_libc/time.c ./tiny_libc/mailbox.c ./tiny_libc/rand.c ./tiny_libc/atol.c
SRC_LIBC_ASM	= $(filter %.S %.s,$(SRC_LIBC))
SRC_LIBC_C	= $(filter %.c,$(SRC_LIBC))

SRC_USER	= ./test/test_shell.elf ./test/rw.elf ./test/fly.elf ./test/consensus.elf ./test/swap.elf

SRC_MAIN	= ${SRC_ARCH} ${SRC_INIT} ${SRC_INT} ${SRC_DRIVER} ${SRC_LOCK} ${SRC_SCHED} ${SRC_MM} ${SRC_SYSCALL} ${SRC_LIBS}

SRC_IMAGE	= ./tools/createimage.c
SRC_ELF2CHAR	= ./tools/elf2char.c
SRC_GENMAP	= ./tools/generateMapping.c

.PHONY:all main bootblock clean

all: elf2char createimage image asm

bootblock: $(SRC_BOOT) riscv.lds
	${CC} ${CFLAGS} -o bootblock $(SRC_BOOT) -e main -Ttext=${BOOTLOADER_ENTRYPOINT}

kernelimage: $(SRC_HEAD) riscv.lds
	${CC} ${CFLAGS} -o kernelimage $(SRC_HEAD) -Ttext=${START_ENTRYPOINT}

payload.c: elf2char main
	./elf2char main > payload.c

user: $(SRC_USER) elf2char generateMapping
	echo "" > user_programs.c
	echo "" > user_programs.h
	for prog in $(SRC_USER); do ./elf2char --header-only $$prog >> user_programs.h; done
	for prog in $(SRC_USER); do ./elf2char $$prog >> user_programs.c; done
	./generateMapping user_programs
	mv user_programs.h include/
	mv user_programs.c kernel/

libtiny_libc.a: $(SRC_LIBC_C) $(SRC_LIBC_ASM) user_riscv.lds
	for libobj in $(SRC_LIBC_C); do ${CC} ${USER_CFLAGS} -c $$libobj -o $${libobj/.c/.o}; done
	for libobj in $(SRC_LIBC_ASM); do ${CC} ${USER_CFLAGS} -c $$libobj -o $${libobj/.S/.o}; done
	${AR} rcs libtiny_libc.a $(patsubst %.c, %.o, $(patsubst %.S, %.o,$(SRC_LIBC)))

$(ARCH_DIR)/crt0.o: $(ARCH_DIR)/crt0.S
	${CC} ${USER_CFLAGS} -c $(ARCH_DIR)/crt0.S -o $(ARCH_DIR)/crt0.o

%.elf : %.c user_riscv.lds libtiny_libc.a $(ARCH_DIR)/crt0.o
	${CC} ${USER_CFLAGS} $< ${USER_LDFLAGS} -o $@

main: $(SRC_MAIN) user riscv.lds

#!/bin/bash
# Build a project subtree in a scratch directory so the repo stays clean.
#
# The checked-in host tools (elf2char/createimage/generateMapping) are mode
# 644 in git and the Makefile hard-codes a cross prefix that does not exist in
# this container, so we copy the tree out and fix both there.  gcc >= 10 also
# defaults to -fno-common, which trips over the generated user_programs.h; the
# original lab toolchain was older, hence -fcommon.
#
# usage: agent_tests/build.sh <ProjectDir> [make target...]
set -u

PROJ="$1"; shift
SRC="/workspace/$PROJ"
DST="/tmp/b/$(echo "$PROJ" | cut -c1-8)"

[ -d "$SRC" ] || { echo "no such project: $SRC"; exit 2; }

rm -rf "$DST"
mkdir -p /tmp/b
cp -a "$SRC" "$DST" || exit 2
chmod +x "$DST"/elf2char "$DST"/createimage "$DST"/generateMapping 2>/dev/null

sed -i 's/^CROSS_PREFIX = .*/CROSS_PREFIX = riscv64-linux-gnu-/' "$DST/Makefile"
sed -i 's/^\(CFLAGS = .*\)$/\1 -fcommon/' "$DST/Makefile"
sed -i 's/^\(USER_CFLAGS = .*\)$/\1 -fcommon/' "$DST/Makefile"

cd "$DST" || exit 2

=== run_tests
#!/bin/bash
# Host-side functional tests for the kernel subsystems implemented in this repo.
#
# Kernel code is compiled natively (with small shims under hostshim/ standing in
# for the RISC-V specific headers) and driven directly, so the scheduling,
# synchronisation, IPC and file-system logic can be executed and asserted on
# without a board or an emulator.
set -u

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
ROOT=$(pwd)
SHIM="$ROOT/agent_tests/hostshim"
OUT=$(mktemp -d)
fail=0

run_case() {
    local name=$1; shift
    if ! gcc -g -O0 -o "$OUT/$name" "$@" 2>"$OUT/$name.log"; then
        echo "[$name] COMPILE FAILED"
        sed -n '1,40p' "$OUT/$name.log"
        fail=1
        return
    fi
    if ! timeout 60 "$OUT/$name"; then
        echo "[$name] RUN FAILED"
        fail=1
    fi
}

P2A="$ROOT/Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part1"
run_case p2a_sched \
    "$ROOT/agent_tests/p2a_sched_test.c" \
    "$P2A/kernel/sched/sched.c" "$P2A/kernel/locking/lock.c" \
    -I"$SHIM" -I"$P2A/include" -I"$P2A/drivers" -I"$P2A/arch/riscv/include"

# get_ticks() reads the RISC-V `time` CSR, which the host cannot execute.  Swap
# just that one read for a counter the test drives; timer_check() -- the code
# actually under test -- is compiled verbatim.
host_time_c() {
    python3 - "$1" "$2" <<'PY'
import sys
src = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
asm = '''    __asm__ __volatile__(
        "rdtime %0"
        : "=r"(time_elapsed));'''
assert asm in src, "get_ticks() no longer looks the way the test expects"
src = src.replace(asm, "    time_elapsed = host_get_ticks();")
src = "extern unsigned long host_get_ticks(void);\n" + src
open(sys.argv[2], "w").write(src)
PY
}

P2B="$ROOT/Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part2"
if [ -f "$ROOT/agent_tests/p2b_sched_test.c" ]; then
    host_time_c "$P2B/kernel/sched/time.c" "$OUT/p2b_time.c"
    run_case p2b_sched \
        "$ROOT/agent_tests/p2b_sched_test.c" \
        "$P2B/kernel/sched/sched.c" "$P2B/kernel/locking/lock.c" \
        "$P2B/kernel/locking/futex.c" "$P2B/kernel/locking/binsem.c" \
        "$OUT/p2b_time.c" \
        -I"$SHIM" -I"$P2B/include" -I"$P2B/drivers" -I"$P2B/arch/riscv/include"
fi

P3="$ROOT/Project3-Interactive_OS_and_Process_Management"
if [ -f "$ROOT/agent_tests/p3_proc_test.c" ]; then
    host_time_c "$P3/kernel/sched/time.c" "$OUT/p3_time.c"
    run_case p3_proc \
        "$ROOT/agent_tests/p3_proc_test.c" \
        "$P3/kernel/sched/sched.c" "$P3/kernel/syscall/mailbox.c" \
        "$P3/kernel/locking/binsem.c" "$P3/libs/string.c" "$OUT/p3_time.c" \
        -I"$SHIM" -I"$P3/include" -I"$P3/drivers" -I"$P3/arch/riscv/include"
fi

P6="$ROOT/Project6-File_System"
if [ -f "$ROOT/agent_tests/p6_fs_test.c" ]; then
    run_case p6_fs \
        "$ROOT/agent_tests/p6_fs_test.c" \
        "$P6/kernel/fs/fs.c" "$P6/kernel/fs/file.c" \
        -I"$SHIM" -I"$P6/include" -I"$P6/drivers" -I"$P6/arch/riscv/include"
fi

rm -rf "$OUT"
if [ "$fail" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "SOME TESTS FAILED"
    exit 1
fi
echo "ALL HOST TESTS PASSED"

#include <asm.h>
#include <csr.h>
#include <asm/sbidef.h>
#include <asm/sbiasm.h>

.section ".entry_function","ax"
ENTRY(_start)
  /* Mask all interrupts */
  csrw CSR_SIE, zero
  csrw CSR_SIP, zero

  /* Disable FPU to detect illegal usage of floating point in kernel space */
  li t0, SR_FS
  csrc sstatus, t0

  /* Load the global pointer */
  .option push
  .option norelax
  la gp, __global_pointer$
  .option pop

  csrr t0, CSR_MHARTID
  bnez t0, secondary
  
  /* Clear BSS for flat non-ELF images */
  la a3, __bss_start
  la a4, __BSS_END__
  ble a4, a3, clear_bss_done
clear_bss:
  sd zero, (a3)
  add a3, a3, RISCV_SZPTR
  blt a3, a4, clear_bss
clear_bss_done:

  /* setup C environment */
  ld tp, core0_tp
  ld sp, kernel_stack_0
  csrw CSR_SSCRATCH, zero

  la a0, riscv_dtb
  sd a1, (a0)

  call main

secondary:
  /* setup C environment */
  ld tp, core1_tp
  ld sp, kernel_stack_1
  csrw CSR_SSCRATCH, zero

  la a0, riscv_dtb
  sd a1, (a0)

  call smp_init

END(_start)

I ran the real `kernel/mm/mm.c` natively (shimmed `pgtable.h`/`sbi.h`, a software Sv39 walker, and the boot-time kernel page table from `arch/riscv/kernel/boot.c`) and replayed the `test/consensus.c` script through it, plus swap round-trips and exit paths.

**What checked out** (verified, not assumed):
- `SHM_VA_BEGIN/END = 0x1000/0xf000` does not collide with the ELF image: `readelf` shows every test ELF's single PT_LOAD at vaddr `0xf000`, largest `memsz 0x3e98` → ends at `0x12e98`, inside `USER_CODE_END 0x14000` that `init_page_table()` pre-maps for `main.c`'s `get_kva_of` loader.
- Attach never returns 0 on success (lowest VA is `0x1000`), and the window-full path correctly releases the frame it speculatively allocated for a fresh key (no leak).
- The consensus sequence works: `get → 0x1000`, `dt`, touch `0x1000` (fault inserts a private frame), `get → 0x2000`. All 9 simulated processes agree on `0x2000`, which matters because `mthread_barrier` keys `binsem_get`/`futex` on the *user VA*.
- Refcounting balances across 9 processes with mixed detach/no-detach exits: frames, pgdir pages and disk slots all return to zero.
- Pinning works (`selete_page()` never returned the shm frame in 200 sweeps); the `1lu << (VPN2_SHIFT+PPN_BITS-1)` bound is exactly the Sv39 user/kernel split (2^38), kernel `stval` goes to `handle_other`; the `_PAGE_SOFT` fault-in path restores content and frees the swap slot, and `free_process_user_page` reclaims slots for still-swapped pages.

The defect is in the "detach an address that is not shared" guard.

findings.title: shm_page_dt() accepts kernel-half addresses; find_pte() walks the kernel's 2MB leaf entries as if they were page tables
findings.detail: shm_page_dt() (line 368) passes the raw user-supplied `addr` straight to find_pte() with no range check, and find_pte() (line 189) tests only `_PAGE_PRESENT` on the level-2/level-1 entries — it never checks for R/W/X, i.e. for a superpage leaf. Every user pgdir contains the kernel window (`pgdir_kva[0x101]` copied by init_page_table), whose level-1 entries 0x80..0xff are 2MB *leaf* mappings of physical 0x50000000-0x60000000. So for a kernel VA the walk descends one level too far and returns `pa2kva(2MB-region base) + vpn0*8` — a pointer at an arbitrary 8-byte word of real memory, which shm_page_dt then interprets as a PTE. Reproduced by running the real mm.c on the host: process 1 attaches key 77 (frame 0x5100c000, count=1); process 0 plants the qword 0x14403001 (PRESENT + pfn of 0x5100c000) at the start of a 2MB-aligned frame it owns (0x51200000) and calls sys_shmpage_dt(0xffffffc051200000). Result: that kernel word is zeroed, shm_page[77].count drops 1->0, and free_user_page() releases the shared frame while process 1's PTE at 0x1000 still points at it — the frame is then handed out to the next alloc_user_page() caller underneath a live mapping. Two lines fix it: reject `addr` outside [SHM_VA_BEGIN, SHM_VA_END) in shm_page_dt(), and make find_pte()/walk_pgdir() bail out when an intermediate entry has any of _PAGE_READ|_PAGE_WRITE|_PAGE_EXEC set.

findings.title: handle_page_fault() silently ignores faults it cannot resolve, so the hart retries the instruction forever
findings.detail: handle_page_fault() (line 395) forwards every user-half stval to alloc_page_helper(), which returns without touching anything when the leaf PTE already has _PAGE_PRESENT (line 216). `cause` is ignored and `regs->sepc` is untouched, so ret_from_exception re-executes the faulting instruction, which faults identically — an endless fault loop with no diagnostic. This is reachable on the normal panic path: entry.S clears SR_SUM on trap entry (`li t0, SR_SUM | SR_FS; csrc sstatus, t0`), and handle_other() then walks the user frame pointer (`while (fp > 0x10000) { prev_ra = *(uintptr_t*)(fp-8); ... }` in kernel/irq/irq.c) with SUM clear. An S-mode access to a U=1 page with SUM=0 raises a load *page* fault whose stval is a mapped user stack address, so handle_page_fault does nothing and the machine wedges after printing the register dump — including for the kernel-address faults this very function routes to handle_other. Same shape for an instruction fetch out of a shared page, which shm_page_get() maps without _PAGE_EXEC (line 353). The handler should treat 'PTE already present' (or a permission mismatch against `cause`) as fatal and call handle_other().

findings.title: Shared-memory keys are folded with `key % SHM_PAGE_NUM` and no key is stored, so distinct keys silently share one page
findings.detail: shm_page_get() (line 337) selects the descriptor with `&shm_page[(uint32_t)key % SHM_PAGE_NUM]` (SHM_PAGE_NUM = 100) and nothing anywhere records which key owns a slot; shm_page_t only holds {count, pa}. Two unrelated programs using keys that are congruent mod 100 — e.g. 42 (consensus's SHMP_KEY) and 142, or 7 and 107 — are handed the same physical frame and the same refcount, so each one sees the other's writes and either can trigger the count==0 free while the other is still attached. mm.c already owns the descriptor table, so a parallel `static int shm_key[SHM_PAGE_NUM];` plus a linear search for a matching-or-free slot (and clearing it when count hits 0 in shm_page_dt/free_process_user_page) removes the aliasing.
